## Week 4: Scores and what they stand for

A score measures one thing and is taken to stand for another. A hospital's risk score predicted next year's medical cost and was used to decide who was offered extra care; at the same cost, Black patients were sicker, so the score flagged fewer of them. A model of a measure with an offset for one group, who it selects and how ill they are, and a noisy measure that flattens a slope. Reinforcement learning: an agent given a reward, and the good we care about. What happens once a score is rewarded: Goodhart's law as an intervention, strategic classification, performative prediction, and a platform that ranked by views.

**Required reading:** [Obermeyer, Powers, Vogeli and Mullainathan, Dissecting racial bias in an algorithm used to manage the health of populations](https://escholarship.org/uc/item/6h92v832) (*Science*, 2019; the abstract and the sections "Health disparities conditional on risk score," "Mechanism of bias" and "Problem formulation," pages 448 to 451) · [Barocas, Hardt and Narayanan, Fairness and Machine Learning, chapter 1: Introduction](https://fairmlbook.org/pdf/fairmlbook.pdf) ("The trouble with measurement" through "Feedback and feedback loops", pages 7 to 14) · skim the Wikipedia article [Goodhart's law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodhart%27s_law)

**Optional:** [Amodei and colleagues, Concrete Problems in AI Safety](https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.06565) (sections 2 and 4) · [YouTube Creator Blog, why we focus on watch time](https://youtubecreator-uk.googleblog.com/2012/09/youtube-now-why-we-focus-on-watch-time.html) (2012) · [Miller, Milli and Hardt, Strategic Classification is Causal Modeling in Disguise](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/miller20b.html) (section 1) · [Perdomo, Zrnic, Mendler-Dünner and Hardt, Performative Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2002.06673) (section 1) · [Jacobs and Wallach, Measurement and Fairness](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.05511) · [Manheim and Garrabrant, Categorizing Variants of Goodhart's Law](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.04585)

**Bring to the class:** one score or algorithm used to make decisions about people, with what it measures and what it stands in for.
